ross-parry-269.description: William Edward Parry's explanatory note on how he rendered Inuktitut sounds in English spelling, with worked examples of each vowel combination, followed by a warning to anyone using the list: Iglulingmiut speakers often answered a question about an object with the name of the material it was made of rather than the name of the article. Show a pair of sealskin mittens and ask what they are, Parry writes, and the answer will probably be "neitiek" (seal) or "amia" (skin), and not "poo-a-look" until you ask again more closely. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-271.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Black to Conjuror
ross-parry-271.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Black, or dark-coloured, it is" at the head of the left column to "Conjuror, or Sorcerer" at the foot of the right, taking in everyday nouns and verbs and birds such as the brent goose (Nui-gluk). William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-272.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Copper to Father-in-law
ross-parry-272.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Copper" (Ka-noo-yak) to "Father (or mother) in-law." William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-273.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Fawn to Heart
ross-parry-273.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Fawn, a" (Noke-wa) to "Heart." William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-274.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Heavy to Lamp of stone
ross-parry-274.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Heavy, it is" to "Lamp of stone." It carries three entries worth singling out: "Hut, or house . . . Igloo," one of the earliest printings of that word in English; "Jacket, upper . . . Cappee-tegga"; and "Lamp of stone . . . Kood-le-ook," the qulliq, the soapstone lamp that is still an emblem of Inuit life in Nunavut. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-276.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Nail of ivory to Rib
ross-parry-276.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Nail of ivory, for stopping the wounds in seals" (Too-noo-ta) to "Rib, small," taking in on the way the ornament of brass or copper worn on the forehead by Iglulingmiut women. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-277.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Rib to Skins of deer
ross-parry-277.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Rib, large" to "Skins of deer, made into a blanket." It holds the specialised terms of the winter hunt: the seal-hole is "Agloo," and the seals are named separately by size and species -- Oguke for the large bearded seal, Neitiek for the small ringed seal, Kairolik for the middle-sized, Ibleeow for the young. The word entered against "Rib, large" is Toolemak, which was also the name of the angakkuq of Igloolik whom George Francis Lyon wrote about at length. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-278.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Skin a rope to Sweat
ross-parry-278.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Skin a rope, he does" to "Sweat, he does," including the spear for large seal (Aklee-ak) and the separate spears for walrus and whale. William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-279.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Swim to Very, or Extremely
ross-parry-279.description: A page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Swim, he does" to "Very, or Extremely," taking in "Too, And, or Also" (Loo), "To-day," the bog blueberry Vaccinium uliginosum, and "Valley, or Low-land." William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.

ross-parry-280.title: Vocabulary of Esquimaux words and sentences: Wait to Young
ross-parry-280.description: The closing page of the Inuktitut-English vocabulary, from "Wait" (Oo-it-tia) and "Walk, he does" through "Whistle, he does" and "White, or any light colour" to "You," singular and plural, and "Young, he is." William Edward Parry compiled the vocabulary with George Francis Lyon over the two winterings, checking words with Iglulingmiut speakers as they were written down.
